'''Ulrich Schwaneberg''' (born 17 June 1969 in [[Waiblingen]], Germany) is a German chemist and protein engineer. He is the Chair of Biotechnology<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biologie.rwth-aachen.de/cms/Biologie/Fachgruppe/Kontakt-und-Lageplaene/Professoren/Interne-Professoren/~bzwc/Prof-Schwaneberg/?lidx=1|title=Prof. Schwaneberg – RWTH AACHEN UNIVERSITY Department of Biology – English|first=Department of|last=Biology|website=www.biologie.rwth-aachen.de|access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> at [[RWTH Aachen University]] and member of the scientific board <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dwi.rwth-aachen.de/index.php?id=368|title=Scientific Board – Team – DWI – Leibniz Institute for Interactive Materials|website=www.dwi.rwth-aachen.de|access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> at the Leibniz Institute for Interactive Materials in Aachen. 
He specializes in directed evolution of proteins for material science applications and on the development of its methodologies. The latter comprise methods for diversity generation (e.g. PLICing,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Blanusa | first1=Milan | last2=Schenk | first2=Alexander | last3=Sadeghi | first3=Hengameh | last4=Marienhagen | first4=Jan | last5=Schwaneberg | first5=Ulrich | title=Phosphorothioate-based ligase-independent gene cloning (PLICing): An enzyme-free and sequence-independent cloning method | journal=Analytical Biochemistry | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=406 | issue=2 | year=2010 | issn=0003-2697 | doi=10.1016/j.ab.2010.07.011 | pages=141–146| pmid=20646988 }}</ref> SeSaM,<ref>{{cite journal | last=Wong | first=T. S. | title=Sequence saturation mutagenesis (SeSaM): a novel method for directed evolution | journal=Nucleic Acids Research | publisher=Oxford University Press (OUP) | volume=32 | issue=3 | date=13 February 2004 | issn=1362-4962 | doi=10.1093/nar/gnh028 | pages=26e–26| pmid=14872057 | pmc=373423 }}</ref> OmniChange,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Dennig | first1=Alexander | last2=Shivange | first2=Amol V. | last3=Marienhagen | first3=Jan | last4=Schwaneberg | first4=Ulrich | editor-last=Marinus | editor-first=Martin G. | title=OmniChange: The Sequence Independent Method for Simultaneous Site-Saturation of Five Codons | journal=PLOS ONE | publisher=Public Library of Science (PLoS) | volume=6 | issue=10 | date=19 October 2011 | issn=1932-6203 |  pmc=3198389 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0026222 | article-number=e26222| pmid=22039444 | bibcode=2011PLoSO...626222D | doi-access=free }}</ref> cepPCR,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Yang | first1=Jianhua | last2=Ruff | first2=Anna J. | last3=Arlt | first3=Marcus | last4=Schwaneberg | first4=Ulrich | title=Casting epPCR (cepPCR): A simple random mutagenesis method to generate high quality mutant libraries | journal=Biotechnology and Bioengineering | publisher=Wiley | volume=114 | issue=9 | date=23 May 2017 | issn=0006-3592 | doi=10.1002/bit.26327 | pages=1921–1927| pmid=28464223 | s2cid=5149806 }}</ref> PePevo<ref name="Rübsam Davari Jakob Schwaneberg p=423">{{cite journal | last1=Rübsam | first1=Kristin | last2=Davari | first2=Mehdi | last3=Jakob | first3=Felix | last4=Schwaneberg | first4=Ulrich | title=KnowVolution of the Polymer-Binding Peptide LCI for Improved Polypropylene Binding | journal=Polymers | publisher=MDPI AG | volume=10 | issue=4 | date=10 April 2018 | issn=2073-4360 | doi=10.3390/polym10040423 | page=423| pmid=30966458 | pmc=6415234 | doi-access=free }}</ref>), as well as high-throughput screening systems (e.g. Fur-Shell).<ref name="Körfer Pitzler Vojcic Martinez p. ">{{cite journal | last1=Körfer | first1=Georgette | last2=Pitzler | first2=Christian | last3=Vojcic | first3=Ljubica | last4=Martinez | first4=Ronny | last5=Schwaneberg | first5=Ulrich | title=In vitro flow cytometry-based screening platform for cellulase engineering | journal=Scientific Reports | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=6 | issue=1 | date=17 May 2016 | issn=2045-2322 | doi=10.1038/srep26128  | doi-access=free| article-number=26128| pmid=27184298 | pmc=4869107 | bibcode=2016NatSR...626128K }}</ref> 
His work group has elucidated general design principles of enzymes by analyzing libraries that contain the full natural diversity of a [[hydrolase]] with single amino acid exchanges and developed strategies to efficiently explore the protein sequence space (e.g. KnowVolution)<ref name="Cheng Zhu Schwaneberg 2015 pp. 9760–9772">{{cite journal | last1=Cheng | first1=Feng | last2=Zhu | first2=Leilei | last3=Schwaneberg | first3=Ulrich | title=Directed evolution 2.0: improving and deciphering enzyme properties | journal=Chemical Communications | publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry (RSC) | volume=51 | issue=48 | year=2015 | issn=1359-7345 | doi=10.1039/c5cc01594d | pages=9760–9772| pmid=25874672 | url=http://publications.rwth-aachen.de/record/466397/files/31_c5cc01594d.pdf }}</ref> and discovered protein engineering principles.

==Career==
Ulrich Schwaneberg studied chemistry at the [[University of Stuttgart]] and received his diploma in 1996. His doctoral studies were also conducted at [[University of Stuttgart]] in the Institute of Technical Biochemistry under the supervision of R. D. Schmid. After his graduation in  July 1999, he joined the lab of [[Frances H. Arnold]] at [[California Institute of Technology]] as post-doctoral fellow for two years. In January 2002, he was appointed as professor at [[Jacobs University Bremen]]. In January 2009, he was appointed as head of the Institute of Biotechnology at RWTH Aachen University and in 2010  co-appointed to the scientific board of directors at the DWI Leibniz Institute for Interactive Materials. Furthermore, he serves on the board of directors in the Bioeconomy Science Center that aims at advancing and focussing research efforts in the area of [[bioeconomy]] in the state of [[North Rhine-Westphalia]] and serves as speaker of the industry lab HICAST ([[Henkel]] Innovation Campus for Advanced and Sustainable Technologies) at RWTH Aachen University<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bio-based.eu/hicast-excellence-for-sustainable-technologies|title=HICAST – Excellence for sustainable technologies – Bio-based News – The portal for bio-based economy & industrial biotechnology|date=22 May 2015|website=bio-based.eu|access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref>

He is a co-inventor on a number of patents of several improved enzymes which have been transferred into industrial use. In 2008, he also co-founded the [[SeSaM-Biotech GmbH]] which offers directed evolution services<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sesam-biotech.com/company/where-we-come-from/|title=Where we come from – SeSaM-Biotech|website=sesam-biotech.com|access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref>
In 2013, he received a visiting professorship for senior international scientists of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], in 2015 a specially appointed professorship at [[Osaka University]], in 2016 the 1.7 M € BMBF award for the Next Generation of Biotechnological Processes and in 2018 the Innovation Award of the BioRegions in Germany for a plant health release technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.innovationspreis-der-bioregionen.de|title=Innovationspreis der BioRegionen in Deutschland 2018 – Wir fördern Ihre innovative Idee!|website=www.innovationspreis-der-bioregionen.de|language=German|access-date=8 June 2018}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
